Incidents Bot: PAGER ALERT: otel-exporter -> honeycomb (eu-west-1) reporting elevated 429/500 responses. 18% error rate over last 5m. auto-page to oncall. thread_ts=2090012345
Alex R: I’m oncall, taking this. seeing the alert in console. any quick customer impact notes?
Emily H: getting inbound tickets: two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, FinSys) reporting missing traces since ~08:12 UTC. severity P2 for AcmeCorp (investigating).
Sanjay P: quick hypothesis: vendor-side throttling / rate-limit change. otel-collector logs show 429 + Retry-After. grabbing headers now.
Alex R: can you paste the excerpts?
Sanjay P: here are raw lines: ```2026-03-15T08:13:02Z otel-collector exporter.go:214 ERROR export failed: status=429 body="rate limited" headers={Retry-After: 30, X-Request-ID: abc123}```
Maya C: thanks. are we seeing corresponding cpu/memory spikes or sudden traffic? Could be sampling change or bad client.
Alex R: infra metrics look steady; request volume to collector is normal. error rate correlates with high payload size spikes from a single service.
Emily H: pushing note to AcmeCorp CSM: "we're investigating trace loss, working on mitigation."
Thomas L: CSMs notified. asking CS to set expectations: missing spans for recent requests, backend logs still present.
Sanjay P: mitigation plan: 1) engage Honeycomb support (ticket created) 2) enable local buffer + exponential backoff on exporter 3) temporarily route traces to S3 for reingest 4) reduce sampling for noisy services 5) if vendor cannot clear, flip to alternate export endpoint (secondary vendor)
Alex R: open ticket to Honeycomb: https://support.honeycomb.io/cases — submitted with request-id abc123 and sample payloads. Honeycomb Support responded: "we're seeing elevated 429s in the EU ingestion cluster, investigating internally."
Incidents Bot: Honeycomb Support posted: "We are aware of elevated ingestion throttling for EU and are rolling config fixes. ETA unknown. Case: HNY-78934"
Maya C: can we enable exporter local buffering? command on collector nodes: ```sudo systemctl set-environment OTEL_EXPORTER_HONEYCOMB_DISABLE=false; echo 'exporter.buffer_dir=/var/otel/buffer' >> /etc/otel/collector.env; systemctl restart otel-collector``` — but better to flip a feature flag in k8s deploy: ```kubectl set env deploy/otel-collector -n observability OTEL_EXPORTER_HONEYCOMB_BACKOFF=extended```
Sanjay P: added note: also bump retries/backoff: OTEL_EXPORTER_HONEYCOMB_RETRIES=10 and increase base backoff to 5s.
Alex R: performing change on canary cluster (2 pods) first. will watch error rate.
Emily H: meanwhile routing quick alert to affected customers: "We have identified a vendor ingestion issue causing intermittent trace delivery; we're buffering and will reingest once vendor stable."
Alex R: canary change applied. watcher shows immediate drop in 429s from canary to 3% but overall cluster still ~16%.
Thomas L: are we comfortable toggling sampling for the noisy service down to 1%? which service is spiking?
Sanjay P: service svc-payments is the culprit, high payloads from trace-heavy debug logging. I'm applying a temporary sampling rule in the collector config: ```processors.batch.action = drop_if_exceeds(1%)``` — applying now.
Alex R: sampling applied. cluster-wide error rate down to ~8% within 7m. exporter latency improved.
Incidents Bot: PagerDuty: oncall escalation to Maya C acknowledged.
Maya C: taking handoff for the next 60 minutes. current state summary: vendor is throttling (HNY-78934), mitigations in place: local buffering enabled on collectors, retries=10/backoff base=5s, svc-payments sampling reduced, canary shows improvement, overall errors down from 18% -> 8%. customers AcmeCorp/FinSys notified.
Alex R: note: we started routing a copy of raw spans to S3 (bucket: s3://redwood-otel-backups/2026-03-15/) for later reingest once vendor clears. command used: ```aws s3 cp /var/otel/buffer/ s3://redwood-otel-backups/2026-03-15/ --recursive``` (process running)
Honeycomb Support: Update: "We've rolled a fix to EU ingestion; throttling should reduce in 10-15m. If you still see 429s after that window, please DM case HNY-78934 with traces. Apologies for the disruption."
Alex R: monitoring shows further improvement; EU ingestion 429s trending down.
Emily H: customer impact update: AcmeCorp saw missing spans for ~36 minutes; FinSys intermittent gaps. CSMs updated.
Sanjay P: action items for post-incident: - formal postmortem (owner: Sanjay P) - evaluate per-service rate limits and sampling defaults - add automated fallback to S3 reingest for exporter backlog - improve alerting to separate vendor-side 429 vs local failures
Maya C: handoff note to next oncall (Tom): please keep vendor ticket HNY-78934 open, confirm no 429s for 30m before re-enabling normal sampling for svc-payments, and don't purge local buffers until we confirm reingest pipeline is ready.
Thomas L: acknowledging handoff, will take over at 09:30 UTC. leaving this thread pinned.
Alex R: closing live paging for now, keeping this incident thread open for postmortem artifacts. thanks everyone for quick coordination :thumbsup:
Maya C: quick check-in: vendor indicates full mitigation; I'm going to keep buffered exports until EOD and schedule reingest run tomorrow morning.
Emily H: will send wrap-up note to impacted customers with timelines and reingest plan.
Incidents Bot: Incident marked as mitigated (partial) at 09:03 UTC. Postmortem owner: Sanjay P.
Alex R: +1 to Sanjay for postmortem. please include timeline, customer impact, and remediation rollout plan.
Maya C: handing back to primary oncall (Alex) at 09:30 UTC — leaving detailed runbook steps in the incident ticket.
Thomas L: confirmed.
Honeycomb Support: Case HNY-78934 closed by vendor with root cause: transient ingestion throttling due to config propagation bug. Recommended long-term: request quota bump or adaptive backoff.
Sanjay P: noted. will include vendor recommendation in follow-up.
Alex R: thanks all. end of thread.
